title: Universality of recursive isomorphism on binary sequences
formal: Is recursive isomorphism on binary sequences universal among countable Borel equivalence relations?
definitions: The space 2^N consists of infinite binary sequences with its product topology and Borel σ-algebra. Set x E_rec y iff there is a total computable bijection π:N→N with y(n)=x(π(n)) for every n. A standard Borel space is a measurable space isomorphic to the Borel space of some Polish space. A countable Borel equivalence relation E on X is a Borel subset of X×X whose equivalence classes are countable. Universality means that for every such (X,E) there exists a Borel function f:X→2^N satisfying x E y iff f(x) E_rec f(y), for all x,y∈X. The map f need not be computable or injective. The requirement holds everywhere, not merely on a conull set for a chosen probability measure.

import_provenance.original_title: Universality of recursive isomorphism on binary sequences
import_provenance.original_statement: Is every countable Borel equivalence relation Borel reducible to recursive isomorphism on 2^omega, where two binary sequences are equivalent when a computable permutation of their coordinates transforms one into the other?
import_provenance.supplied_caveat: Remark: Editorial continuation of Hjorth’s joint universality results: universality on five-symbol sequences, and subsequently three-symbol sequences, is established; the binary case and its merely measure-universal version must be distinguished.

context_blocks.text: Marks proves universality on a three-symbol alphabet and measure universality on the binary alphabet, while distinguishing full binary universality.

sentences: Binary sequences are equivalent when a computable permutation rearranges their coordinates.
The comparison objects are Borel equivalence relations with countable classes.
A reduction must preserve and reflect equivalence on every pair.
The reduction may be any Borel function.
Measure universality and universality on three symbols do not settle the binary target.
